title: Grandma's Recipe Is In My HANDWRITING
premise: In a town where the night you finally cook a recipe right its card flies off to whoever needs it most, my grandma's sixty-year-old soup card is in my handwriting, and I've never written it. So I copy it and cook it myself, all spring, until my own card starts tugging toward the window.
twist: When I finally cook her soup right, my copy flies out the window and lands sixty years back in nineteen-year-old Grandma's soup pot, so she learned it from my card and I learned it from hers: nobody ever invented the soup.
world: Grandma Nell's butter-yellow kitchen with robin's-egg blue cabinets, a copper pot, a bowl of lemons, a dented tin on a shelf and a framed old photo, in a pink-gold town at dusk.
